bullets.text: We will replace the two existing AHUs with high-efficiency units ≥12,000 m³/h and rotary heat recovery certified ≥70%, following the weekend changeover pattern proven at Riverside Leisure Centre.
Occupied adjoining rooms will be tempered with temporary AHUs to hold 18–22°C during construction, as specified.
South façade glazing will use double-glazed units targeting Uw ≤1.4 W/m²K on retained mullions, with shrink-wrap weather protection — method reused from Oakwood School.
Sports floor installation will follow our Class P1 QC hold-points (moisture, rebound, colour match under 4000K).
Roof plant crane lifts will use our temporary works pack: Chartered designer, 110% trial lift, exclusion zones.
Waste diversion target ≥75% with monthly registers, exceeding the 70% requirement.
Reference 1 — Riverside Leisure HVAC upgrade (2024), $920k, 11 weeks, heat recovery 72%.
Reference 2 — Oakwood School sports hall envelope (2023), $640k, Uw 1.2 glazing, zero incidents.
Supporting reference — Harborview Arena finishes (2022) for Class P1 sports surface delivery.
HVAC may be partly subcontracted under our approved supply-chain controls; any package >20% will be declared.
Project Manager: Samira Haddad — 11 years public building works; available full-time from November 2026.
Site Supervisor: Tomasz Lewandowski — façade and temporary weatherproofing lead on Oakwood.
HVAC Lead: Priya Nair — commissioning engineer for heat-recovery AHU packages.
Insurance exceeds minima: PL $10M / PI $3M for temporary works design.
We commit to a maximum 14-week continuous hall closure with changing-rooms handover at week 8.
Weather contingency of 8 working days is embedded on the façade critical path.
Parallel working: façade W3–6 and HVAC risers W3–8, commissioning W13, snagging W14.
Price schedule will be completed without altering item codes; arithmetical checks welcomed.
Any heat-recovery technology variant will be priced only on schedule tab V, if selected in the form.
